brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Compartmentalized storage for small sewing supplies (threads, buttons, needles, etc.)
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments), and notch:0#-1,1#notch0 hex-bin-notch-mf-div2 provides 4 cells total with 9 sub-compartments for sorting notions by type/color

requirements.requirement: Hooks/handling for tools (scissors, tape measures) and thread/ribbon organization
requirements.evidence: accessory:0#0,0#1 hex-acc-hook provides double hooks on cell flat for hanging scissors/tape; accessory:0#0,0#2 hex-acc-comb provides cable comb teeth usable as thread/ribbon comb to keep spools and trims ordered; accessory:0#0,1#0 hex-acc-anchor allows wall/ground anchoring for stability

requirements.requirement: Compact, stable cluster that passes configurator checks
requirements.evidence: 3-piece L-shaped cluster (0,0,0; 0,1,0; 1,0,0) with meshClash clear, no error issues; only expected warnings: LOOSE_BODY and OPEN_CAP_FACE info

finish.summary: Built a compact 3-cell sewing organizer: two 2-compartment bins + one 3-compartment bin + a 2-compartment notch bin in the valley for 9 sorting spaces, plus a hook plate for scissors/tools and a cable comb for threads/ribbons. All meshes clear and ready for tabletop use; can be wall-mounted via the anchor if desired.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Port plug
parts.use: Blanks a side port you are not using, so a cell that is closed up looks finished and nothing gets in through a hole you left open.

parts.name: Port louvre
parts.use: Vents a closed cell without letting rain in, so a box that has to breathe can still stand outside.

parts.name: Port screen
parts.use: Passes air and keeps insects and debris out, so a cell can breathe through an opening that is still covered.

parts.name: Port hose barb
parts.use: Lands a hose on a cell, so water arrives and leaves through a spigot drawn for it rather than over an edge.

parts.name: Port cable plate
parts.use: Leads cable through a side port on finished holes, so wiring enters a closed cell through something drawn for it and each run has its own way in.

parts.name: Blank plug
parts.use: Fills an insert recess you are not using, so the face reads flat and the pocket stays clean.

parts.name: Female socket
parts.use: Seats in a recess and takes a stud, which makes it the bottom of every stacked insert.

parts.name: Male stud
parts.use: Threads through a seated socket and stands proud of the face, so it can carry whatever mounts above it.

parts.name: Foot
parts.use: Snaps onto a stud to give the face something to stand on, so a cell can rest on its cover rather than on its rim.

parts.name: Zip-tie anchor
parts.use: Seats in a recess and gives a cable tie something to pass through, so a bundle is anchored to the face instead of looped around it.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
